title: Tuesday Quick Tip
subtitle: How many drills
hook: How many drills did you run at your last practice?
intro: Kids barely learn one before the next starts.
statement: Fewer drills can mean more learning.
q1: Do you run three or four drills done well —
q2: or many short drills to keep things moving?
q3: Which drill did kids actually get better at?
t1: Both can work. But skills stick
t2: when kids have time to repeat them.
cta: Coaches — how many drills do you plan?
ctaLines: Three drills and a game. Six short ones. It depends.
Fewer and deeper or more and quicker?
ctaPrompt: Share your planning habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
How many drills did you run at your last practice?
The plan has eight drills. Kids barely learn one before the next starts.
Fewer drills can mean more learning.
A few drills done well or many short ones. Every team is different.
How many drills do you plan? Share your habit in the comments.
